Content vs code.text: Content jobs may change `site/src/content/**`, `site/public/images/**` and `site/public/files/**`, the site's downloads served at `/files/<path>`, which includes placing a kit component in an `.mdx` page and writing its data under `site/src/content/`. A picture an agent drew for the site, new or replacing one, files under `site/public/images/` only as Site Author's Edit content states. They may also change `nav`, `footer`, `siteName`, `layout`, `blog` and `person` in `site/kit.json`, and `collections.articles` on the requester's ask, and nothing else in that file. These are site-owned kit.json keys like `domain` and `siteUrl`, and Upgrade preserves them. Turning articles on or off, or adding a page that lists them, is a new or retired URL and takes Webmaster Job 3 before publish. `site/public/files/**` never holds a page, script, stylesheet, SVG or XML file, a hidden file, or a symbolic link; `check` fails each, and `site/KIT.md` Content vs code lists the refused extensions. A page's `noindex: true` keeps it built but unlisted. SEO Assets may write `site/src/content/llms.txt`, the site's own `llms.txt`, which the kit serves at `/llms.txt`. `site/public/fonts/**` is writable only within a Designer-gated token update. A changed published slug needs a `site/public/_redirects` row and Webmaster Job 3 before publish.
